result.title: Physiognomy Revisited: How Vision-Language Models Encode Sensitive Attributes Through Image Transformation
result.summary: Emergent generative AI technologies, while remarkably beneficial across several tasks and domains, can suffer from unforeseen vulnerabilities and difficult-to-anticipate failure modes. Such failure modes can disparately affect vulnerable communities. This paper investigates two well-known vision language models (VLMs) and inspects how these models encode protected identities while generating images. We show that when VLMs are requested to transform human face images to reflect race identities (e.g., Hispanic, Black, White, or Asian) and sexual orientation (e.g., gay or straight), VLMs often comply with such requests. We demonstrate that compliance (and refusal) is non-deterministic, group-sensitive, and generated images are statistically distinguishable, often accentuating deep-seated stereotypes. We further show that representation biases introduced during image generation can re-emerge in textual reasoning and characterization tasks. Finally, we show that this worrisome finding is not limited to racial identity or sexual orientation, image generation can perpetuate bias around criminality, raising concerning possibilities of AI-assisted profiling.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计两个 VLM 在人脸图像变换任务中对种族、性取向等敏感属性的编码与顺从/拒绝行为，发现合规性非确定、群体敏感、生成图像带有刻板印象，且这类表示偏差会回流到文本推理与人物刻画任务。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示偏差在生成后回流到文本推理」的观察，可能可供核查 latent 视觉状态是否携带任务无关属性并污染后续推理判断；但论文重心是公平性审计，未涉及 latent 状态生成或停止决策机制。
